subject: general
question: A shopkeeper marked his goods at X% above their cost price and sold them at a discount of 16%. If he gained 68% profit, then find the value of X.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the relationship: **MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)**.

MP ÷ CP = (100 + 68) ÷ (100 − 16) = 168 ÷ 84 = 2 ÷ 1.

Since **MP is 2** and **CP is 1**, the markup is 1 unit over 1 unit of CP.

Markup percentage X = (1 ÷ 1) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Discount% = 16%, Profit% = 68%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100 | MP = CP × (100 + X%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ea60d8216b118b92785ef44d1dd8d1445880992d0fb622596b3c35ec203b149.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 68 = 168.

⇒ Since **Discount** is 16%, SP = 84% of **Marked Price (MP)**.

⇒ 84% of MP = 168 ⇒ MP = (168 ÷ 84) × 100 = 200.

⇒ **Markup Value** = MP − CP = 200 − 100 = 100.

⇒ **Markup Percentage (X)** = (100 ÷ 100) × 100 = 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Marked Price is the price printed on the label. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price**: SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

The direct ratio **MP/CP = (100 + P%)/(100 − D%)** is derived by equating the two SP formulas.</p
